headline: Mexican peso falls 1.3% to October low amid unwinding carry trades
summary: The Mexican peso fell 1.3% to about 18.67 per US dollar, reaching its weakest close for the month as carry trades unwound and geopolitical risks rose.
why: Emerging market currencies are sensitive to shifts in global risk sentiment, geopolitical tensions, and changes in speculative positioning like carry trades.

impacts.name: Mexican Peso
impacts.why: Unwinding carry trades and rising Middle East risk drove investors away from emerging market currency exposure.

why_moved: A combination of rising Middle East risks and a broader unwinding of carry trades reduced demand for emerging market assets.
